_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRUNED BY THE 9/3 OPEN, AND THIS TIME SOMETHING WAS ACTUALLY REMOVED. THE AVGO ROW IS GONE: it reported 2026-09-02 after the close as the row said it would, and the print is now VERIFIED COMPLETE on a live per-symbol pull - fiscal Q3 2026, actual 3.32 against the 3.16 estimate the row carried, a 5.1% beat. The 9/2 pre-close explicitly assigned this removal to this run and it is discharged. WHAT THE ROW ACCOMPLISHED, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DELETED: its branch one bound any semiconductor or enterprise-software entry whose five-session time stop crossed 9/2, and it was checked and found not to bind the MDT entry on 9/2 because a medical-device maker carries no read-through from a semiconductor print. Its branch three - that a hard AVGO gap on 9/2 must not be traded on the 9/3 reaction bar - IS BINDING RIGHT NOW AND WAS OBEYED THIS MORNING: AVGO beat and was SOLD 5.68% to 346.34 bid, and it is refused today on exactly the pre-commitment written six sessions early. That is a branch written before it cost anything and honoured on the morning it applied, which is the whole reason the file works that way. ORCL 2026-09-10 pm IS ADDED IN ITS PLACE, quoted live at 148.33 bid / 148.40 ask at 13:49:50Z, with ADBE reporting the same evening at 289.06 bid. Written now, five sessions early and with nothing at stake, for the same reason the AVGO branches were: a pre-commitment made on the morning it binds is not a pre-commitment. The branch matters concretely because today's MDT specification carries a 9/10 TIME STOP - the same date - so any future enterprise-software or database entry sized on this account will meet a written rule rather than an improvised one. TONIGHT'S NINE-NAME CLUSTER IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED AS ROWS and the reasoning is the file's own: ZS, DOCU, LULU, PATH, IOT, ASAN, GWRE, AMBA and PL all report after today's close, and a row enters this file when a branch can be decided in advance for it, not because a date exists. No position and no candidate sits in that complex - GTLB and BOX were both refused this morning partly on it - and adding nine rows with nothing behind them would be noise wearing the shape of diligence. The cluster is recorded in state.json where the refusals live. impliedMove on the ORCL row is NULL BECAUSE NO STRADDLE WAS PULLED, which is correct rather than an omission: item 3 is owed before an earnings HOLD, the book is flat, no position exists that could carry through 9/10, and a number this board did not pull does not exist. It becomes owed the moment a position exists that would cross the print.

ADBE REPORTS THE SAME EVENING - fiscal Q3 2026, 2026-09-10, pm, verified true, estimate 5.83, no actual - quoted live at 289.06 bid / 289.79 ask, +3.31% against a 279.79 close, and it is named here rather than given its own row because the two share one date and one branch. THE DATE MATTERS TO A POSITION THIS BOARD MAY ACTUALLY HOLD: today's MDT specification carries a 9/10 time stop, the same day, though MDT is a medical-device maker and takes no read-through from either name - checked rather than assumed, the same way the AVGO row was checked against MDT on 9/2 and found not to bind. impliedMove is NULL because no straddle was pulled and none is owed: the book is flat and item 3 binds before a HOLD, not before a watch. A number this board did not pull does not exist.

branches.cond: An entry considered in ORCL or ADBE themselves, or in an enterprise-software, database or cloud sympathy name, whose five-session time stop would carry it through 2026-09-10
branches.act: Refused unless the position is sized and stopped to survive the gap, or is closed before the print by a run that says so explicitly at entry
branches.why: The same arithmetic that refused AVGO on 9/2 and SMCI on 8/12, written forward to the date rather than rediscovered on the morning of 9/9. A -8% equity stop does not survive an event gap: the realistic bad case gaps THROUGH the exit rather than filling at it, so the stop is decorative and the real risk is the implied move, unpriced. The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright. The escape clause is named so it is a branch rather than a blanket ban - a position may be opened if it is deliberately closed before the print, and the run that opens it must write that intention down AT ENTRY rather than discover the conflict on 9/9. Note the concrete reach of this: an entry opened any day from 9/3 to 9/10 with a five-session stop lands on or after this date, so this branch binds essentially every enterprise-software entry available for the next week.

branches.cond: ORCL or ADBE gaps hard on 9/11 and the 9/11 open wants to trade the reaction
branches.act: Not on the reaction bar - the day-2 or day-3 pullback that HOLDS ITS PRE-PRINT CLOSE is the entry, and item 2 governs
branches.why: Written five sessions early because the version of this branch on the AVGO row was obeyed this morning and is the reason AVGO was refused at -5.68% rather than argued about. The record this board now has is unusually clean on the point: SAIC lost its 125.96 pre-print close on day 2 and was refused twice; NTNX the same; OLLI was PRE-REGISTERED on 9/2 as worth buying if it held, and on 9/3 it sat below both its 72.34 pre-print close and its own reaction-bar low and was refused; MDT held 1.53% above its line and is the one that was bought. The test is not whether the gap fades - MDT's faded hard - it is whether it holds the pre-print close. Nine names report tonight and more on 9/10, so this branch will be reached repeatedly.
